data.name: Andromada
data.short_meaning: In Greek mythology, Andromeda was a beautiful princess chained to a rock as a sacrifice to a sea monster.
data.long_meaning: Andromeda was the name of a beautiful princess in Greek mythology, daughter of Cassiopeia and Cepheus. She was punished by the gods for boasting about her beauty. To appease the sea god Poseidon, her mother was forced to sacrifice her to a sea monster. The monster was averted, however, when Perseus arrived and saved Andromeda, making her his wife.

seo.description_paragraph: Andromeda is a Greek name with a rich history and cultural significance. In Greek mythology, she was a beautiful princess, the daughter of Cassiopeia and Cepheus. Her boastful words about her beauty angered the gods, leading to her punishment in the form of a prophecy: a sea monster would destroy her home, and only her sacrifice could save her people. Andromeda was chained to a rock as a sacrifice, but her fate was changed when Perseus arrived and saved her, making her his wife.
